dedupe_keys.name: piano key weirs for flood risk management at hydropower dams in france edf malarce dam

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study presents the Piano Key Weir, an overflow spillway developed by the Hydro Engineering Centre of EDF to release water safely from dams during heavy rain. Hydropower is about 20 percent of installed capacity in France, and more intense precipitation and faster snowmelt are expected to raise flood risk, overtopping and outages at dams. Updated EDF hydrological studies showed extreme floods becoming more frequent, and the weir increases discharge capacity without raising the maximum reservoir level. At the Malarce dam in the Chassezac valley, Ardeche, 28.4 m high with a 16 MW plant commissioned in 1968, the weir added about 600 cubic metres per second for a total of 4,600. The first weir was built at the Goulours dam from 2003 to 2005; weirs are now in 10 French dams and about 30 installations worldwide, helped by the choice not to patent the design. Costs range from 200,000 euros to a few million per dam, with little maintenance and no operators. The page, published in 2018 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML. Coverage is France with global uptake. Caveats: suitability varies by dam and approval takes long. It illustrates spillway capacity retrofits for dam flood safety and hydropower resilience studies. Related records: case_study-iceland-landsvirkjun-glacier-melt-hydropower covers reservoir management under changing inflows.
